- If sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change within 2–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast deviates > 3% from 10-day moving average, adjust toward it.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 7–10 days); reduce final 5–7 days by 1–3% to match true outcome.
